title: Hymn and Choir
premise: Mara Joubert, a pest controller who prides himself on never believing in anything, is hired to deal with an infestation at a rural excavation site where workers have begun hearing a choir under the floorboards. When the crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, Mara discovers the fingerprints on the walls belong to people who vanished in 1974 — including his own grandmother, whose disappearance the family never spoke of. The thing beneath the site collects voices, and it has been waiting for someone with her blood to return what was taken: a hymnal buried with the door. To survive, Mara must stop disbelieving long enough to sing back, giving the frost-bound dead their names again before winter's final pattern seals him inside with them.
about_author: Juniper Villalobos grew up in the high desert towns of the American Southwest, where abandoned mines and sealed wells were playground hazards and local legends alike. Their fiction explores how families keep secrets the way old houses keep cold — stubbornly, and always leaking somewhere.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Mara takes a pest control job at the Kestrel Hollow excavation site, annoyed by the foreman's talk of 'something singing.' In the break room he finds claw-like scratch marks and greasy fingerprints too high on the wall for any animal. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: dry skepticism masking a lifetime of learned silence about his family.

chapters.title: Frost in July
chapters.summary: Mara returns alone and finds frost blooming indoors despite summer heat, tracing patterns like sheet music across the windows. A night watchman tells him the crew hears a choir under the floor after dark. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession; the first crack in his disbelief.

chapters.title: What the Crew Unearthed
chapters.summary: The excavation crew breaks through to a stone door, its hinges fused, sealed from the inside with mortar mixed with hair. That night two workers quit; one leaves a voicemail reciting a hymn he says he never learned. POV: alternating Mara and foreman Delia Okafor. Emotional beat: dread arriving as bureaucratic inconvenience.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hymnal
chapters.summary: Mara's mother lets slip that his grandmother Odile vanished in 1974 near Kestrel Hollow, leaving behind a hymnal with pages torn out. Mara recognizes the frost patterns as matching its marginalia. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; identity beginning to shift from skeptic to inheritor.

chapters.title: The Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Forensics-minded Delia matches the wall prints to missing persons from 1974 — eleven sets, all belonging to the church congregation that dissolved that year. The prints are fresh. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: rational frameworks straining against evidence that refuses to stay past tense.

chapters.title: Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Mara crawls beneath the site office and finds a cavity lined with frost and hundreds of small objects: rings, dentures, a child's shoe. Something breathes in the dark without lungs. He retreats, bleeding from scratches he doesn't remember getting. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: terror breaking through professional detachment.

chapters.title: Voices on Tape
chapters.summary: Delia plays site recordings: beneath machinery noise, a choir sings a hymn no archive contains, and one voice is unmistakably Mara's. He was recorded saying words he never spoke. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: violation — the thing isn't haunting the site, it's rehearsing him.

chapters.title: The 1974 File
chapters.summary: In county records Mara finds the congregation's last service was interrupted mid-hymn; the minister's report describes 'a door opening inward where there was no door.' Eleven names, one crossed out and rewritten in different ink: Odile Joubert. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the past becoming personal geography.

chapters.title: Cold Snap
chapters.summary: An unseasonal frost kills the site's power. Workers abandon the project; Delia stays. Frost now spreads outward from the dig in perfect concentric rings, like ripples. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: loyalty versus self-preservation; choosing to stay beside a stranger.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Mara's mother finally opens Odile's hymnal: the torn pages were cut by hand, and tucked in the binding is a photograph of the congregation posed before an unmarked stone doorway. On the back: 'We gave it our voices so it would take nothing else.' POV: Mara. Emotional beat: understanding dawning — the sealing was a bargain, not a prison.

chapters.title: It Learns My Name
chapters.summary: At night the choir begins singing responses to Mara when he speaks aloud, harmonizing with his voice, then replacing it. His reflection frosts over and mouths along a half-second late. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: horror of dissolution — the thing is learning to be him.

chapters.title: Delia's Confession
chapters.summary: Delia admits she took this contract deliberately: her father was the 1974 minister's organist, and she grew up humming a hymn she couldn't source. She believes they are both descendants of the bargain. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: found family forming between two people bound by inherited debt.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Deciphering the marginalia, Mara learns the ritual: the congregation fed the thing their voices to seal it, but Odile stole the hymnal — the anchor — dooming the seal to decay. It must be returned, sung, not just placed. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Inward
chapters.summary: Mara and Delia breach the door and find a chapel mirrored underground, pews facing a pulpit of ice, frost etched with eleven kneeling figures. The choir falls silent as they enter — listening. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: awe curdling into the sense of walking into a mouth.

chapters.title: Odile's Voice
chapters.summary: Among the kneeling figures, one turns: a woman wearing Odile's face, preserved in frost, mouthing the torn hymn's missing verse. She points at the pulpit, then at Mara's chest — the hymnal isn't enough; it needs a living voice freely given. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love and horror entwined; recognizing kin in the monstrous.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Delia argues they can reseal it with recordings, machines, anything but themselves. Testing it, they play the tape into the chapel; the frost simply absorbs the sound and grows hungrier, cracking toward the surface town. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: the collapse of every workaround; sacrifice becomes unavoidable.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Mara understands the theme of the thing's hunger: it doesn't want voices, it wants to belong to something — it collects because it was excluded from the congregation's God. He begins composing an answer rather than a surrender. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: empathy as strategy; the monster reframed as the loneliest thing alive.

chapters.title: First Verse
chapters.summary: Mara sings the restored hymn at the pulpit, offering his voice line by line while Delia holds the hymnal open. The frost figures rise and join in, and the chapel stops being hungry — for one verse, it is a congregation again. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: transcendence inside terror; belonging achieved at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: The Taking
chapters.summary: The thing accepts the gift and begins drawing Mara's voice out entirely; Delia refuses to close the book, instead writing her own name beside his, splitting the claim. The frost recoils from a freely shared bond it cannot parse or own. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: climax of found family — refusing to let another be taken alone.

chapters.title: Final Pattern
chapters.summary: With two names given and the hymnal returned to the pulpit, the frost writes its final pattern: eleven figures plus two, then dissolving into clean water. The chapel collapses gently inward, sealing itself forever. Mara's voice returns hoarse but his own. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: release; grief and gratitude indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Sung
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the site is quietly filled in. Mara hums without realizing it — fragments of the hymn remain, harmless now, more memory than haunting. Delia visits with her father's organ music; they compare notes like survivors of the same hometown. POV: Delia. Emotional beat: quiet healing; belief arrived at, not forced.

chapters.title: Coda: The Open Page
chapters.summary: Mara mails the recovered hymnal to his mother with one page left intentionally blank. In the epilogue's last image, frost blooms briefly on her kitchen window in a pattern resembling a rest between notes — patient, unhurried, at peace. POV: Mara's mother. Emotional beat: legacy transformed; the family's silence finally given a melody.
